title: Reflex merit lifecycle: like-rise, sink, archive-to-ref after a week, re-discovery validates
desc: The self-curating law of the living-reflex tree. --like promotes a proven step UP in a core T1 skill (merit-rank; like-count is wkhippo-derived only on demand, never stored). Low-merit steps sink; a step stuck at the bottom of core for over a week is removed from core and moved to the T3 -ref archive. If a newly-added step matches one already in -ref, that independent re-discovery certifies it a genuinely-needed reflex and it is promoted back. Darwinian knowledge selection; signal auto-separates from noise. User-articulated 2026-07-14.
steps: PHASE 1 RISE (the original intent): wkappbot skill edit ID --like FRAGMENT promotes the matched step UP toward the top of a core T1 reflex skill. Purpose: keep the important, proven-in-practice reflexes at the TOP where on-load and agent-brief surface them FIRST. The reorder itself IS the merit signal -- there is NO stored like-counter. The like-COUNT is wkhippo-DERIVED only WHEN NEEDED (a lazy transcript search over real skill-like commands, dedup by session), never persisted. So --like has two faces: an immediate cheap reorder (always), and an on-demand verifiable count (only when someone asks). Sibling: --dislike sinks a step.

PHASE 2 SINK plus PHASE 3 ARCHIVE: --dislike, or simply never earning a like, lets a step drift toward the BOTTOM of its core skill. MAINTENANCE RULE: a step that has sat at the bottom of a core T1 skill for more than a WEEK is judged low-merit -- REMOVE it from CORE and MOVE it into the sibling T3 -ref skill. This keeps core lean and high-signal (the top is what matters, surfaced first) while LOSING NOTHING -- the -ref skill is the archive of record. Implement as a periodic sweep (a gg maintenance-step candidate) that finds bottom-parked-over-a-week steps and relocates them from core to ref.

PHASE 4 RESURRECTION equals VALIDATION (the elegant part): when a NEW step is added to a core skill, CHECK the sibling -ref archive for the SAME reflex by content-fragment match. If -ref ALREADY holds that reflex, the fact that a later independent session RE-DISCOVERED and re-added it PROVES it is a GENUINELY-NEEDED reflex -- a real recurring need, not the one-off noise that was correctly archived. Action: certify it, promote it back into core as a VALIDATED reflex, and note the re-discovery. Recurrence is the truth test: noise is added once and never returns; a true reflex keeps coming back.

TIE-IN to the post-delegation reflex procedure (this lifecycle is its SIGNAL LAYER): RISE trigger = delegation-completion-reflex-like-spec (proven-useful reflexes earn a like on delegation SUCCESS). New-step source = agent-failure-reflection-gate (a failure forces a reflection edit, adding a step that may later resurrect-validate). Static-findability complement = skill-search-coverage-guide (coverage score answers can it be FOUND; this merit-lifecycle answers does it DESERVE the top slot -- two orthogonal axes that compose). Mechanics = skill-edit-step-ordering-spec (--like/--dislike/move/swap). Philosophy = knowledge-ification-procedure-jisikhwa (the living tree that grows AND prunes itself).

WHY (Opus synthesis): this is Darwinian selection for knowledge. Reflexes that recur and get liked RISE and persist at the top; unused ones SINK and archive to ref after a week; archived-then-rediscovered ones are CERTIFIED true. Signal (recurring, liked, re-discovered) auto-separates from noise (added once, never liked, never re-hit) with NO human curator deciding value -- lived practice decides. The tree stays lean where it is read most (core top) and forgets nothing (ref archive). STATUS 2026-07-14: user-articulated. Core team is building --like/--dislike (rise/sink). Two automation pieces remain to build: (a) the over-a-week bottom-parked archive sweep from core to ref; (b) the on-add-step resurrection check against the sibling -ref.

PHASE 5 STATIC TIER (the protection line -- user 2026-07-14): a core skill carries a DIVIDER LINE. Steps ABOVE the divider are STATIC reflexes -- PINNED, essential, archive-IMMUNE: the over-a-week sink/archive sweep NEVER touches them regardless of their like/read recency, because they are foundational laws that must always fire. Steps BELOW the divider are DYNAMIC reflexes -- the churn frontier governed by PHASES 1-4 (like-rise, dislike-sink, archive-to-ref after a week, resurrect on re-discovery). GRADUATION PATH: a dynamic reflex that earns RESURRECTION-VALIDATION (PHASE 4 -- independently re-discovered and re-added after having been archived) has PROVEN it is genuinely needed, so it graduates ABOVE the divider into the STATIC tier, where it can never be swept out again. So the tree has two zones: a stable STATIC core (proven-true, pinned above the line, permanent) and a DYNAMIC frontier (below the line, where new reflexes compete on merit until they either prove themselves and graduate up, or fade down to the -ref archive). This is how the tree keeps its hard-won essentials FOREVER while still letting the frontier churn -- essential reflexes are protected by structure (position above the line), not by luck of recent use.

PHASE 1 CEILING (user 2026-07-14): --like raises a step UP but is CEILING-CAPPED -- it RECOGNIZES the === divider line and any [PIN] step and CANNOT lift a step above them. A dynamic step climbs on likes only up to the position just BELOW the nearest divider or [PIN] above it. CONSEQUENCE: likes churn the DYNAMIC frontier but can NEVER disturb the STATIC tier order -- the only way a step crosses ABOVE the divider is GRADUATION via resurrection-validation (PHASE 4 plus 5), never raw like-count. So === and [PIN] are HARD STRUCTURAL CEILINGS: they protect essential reflexes both from REMOVAL (archive-immune, PHASE 5) AND from being reordered or displaced by frontier like-churn (this step). Structure protects the essentials on two axes at once -- position and permanence.

ARCHITECTURE SPLIT (user 2026-07-14 correction -- mechanics vs policy): wkappbot CORE (appbot) owns ONLY the PRIMITIVES -- skill edit --like/--dislike as a reorder that RECOGNIZES the === divider and [PIN] ceilings (PHASE 1), plus the step move/swap verbs. The LIFECYCLE AUTOMATION is HARNESS work (THIS wkappbot-kih repo, in wkharness-* hooks/tools), because it is HARNESS POLICY -- exactly like every other reflex/guard here: (a) the over-a-week bottom-parked archive sweep core to ref (PHASE 3); (b) the on-add-step resurrection check against the sibling -ref (PHASE 4); (c) graduation-to-STATIC enforcement (PHASE 5). The harness owns the POLICY KNOBS -- how long is too long, what counts as a re-discovery content match, what earns graduation above the line -- because policy is the harness's job, never the core CLI's. So the remaining build lands HERE in the harness, NOT in appbot core. CORE gives the verbs; the HARNESS enforces the law. This mirrors the whole repo: appbot provides skill/file/edit primitives, wkappbot-kih is the reflex nervous system that decides WHEN and WHETHER they fire.

TRIGGER equals SCORE PRESSURE, not necessarily a cron (user 2026-07-14): the archive/curation does NOT need a standalone timed sweep. As --add-steps PILE UP, a skill bloats and its knowledge-ification / diet / coverage SCORE drops, at which point the HARNESS already DEMANDS a score improvement (the same pressure as the CLAUDE.md diet-score guard). That demand IS the curation trigger: the MODEL (the intelligence) then MANUALLY applies this lifecycle -- sink and move the stale bottom steps to -ref, graduate any resurrection-validated ones above the divider, respect the === and [PIN] ceilings. So PHASE 3/4/5 run as HARNESS-PRESSURE-TRIGGERED MANUAL CURATION by the model, not necessarily as coded automation. The harness supplies the PRESSURE (the score-drop demand); the model supplies the JUDGMENT (which steps are stale vs essential -- a judgment call a cron cannot make well). This is WHY the lifecycle is a SPEC/PROCEDURE the model follows, not merely a script: deciding what is truly essential vs noise needs intelligence. The harness's only job is to FORCE that curation to happen the moment bloat crosses the line -- mechanics and pressure from the harness, judgment from the model. Fittingly, THIS skill will itself hit that pressure as it grows and get curated by the same rule it describes.

TIER-AWARE --like (the -howto rule, user 2026-07-14): --like behaves differently per 3-tier level because ORDER MEANS a different thing in each. T1 CORE: step order encodes MERIT (importance-ranked), so --like safely reorders within the frontier (below the === / [PIN] ceiling). T2 -HOWTO: step order encodes TIME / EXECUTION SEQUENCE -- do step 1, THEN 2, THEN 3, a procedure. Reordering a procedure by merit would CORRUPT the sequence, so a -howto is BY DEFAULT treated as order-critical: --like FAILS on a -howto that has NO divider line. To make part of a -howto merit-reorderable you must add an explicit === divider that carves out a non-sequential zone; only steps in that zone accept --like, while the sequential steps stay locked in execution order. T3 -ref: the archive -- order is least critical (reference lookup); it just holds demoted-then or validated reflexes. RULE OF THUMB: --like is SAFE where order encodes IMPORTANCE (core), and REFUSED where order encodes TIME (a howto with no divider) -- because a merit vote must never silently scramble a step-by-step procedure. The === divider is the explicit opt-in that declares this region is importance-ordered, not time-ordered, and is therefore safe to reorder.

SCORE THRESHOLD -- RE-VERIFIED FROM CANONICAL CODE 2026-07-14 (corrects TWICE: the user 20-anchor memory was RIGHT, and my first correction read the WRONG function). The edit-gate skill score is Get-WkSkillBaseScore into Get-WkSkillStructScore in wkharness-common-skilllock.ps1 -- NOT Get-WkTierScore in wkharness-common-tier.ps1, which is the OLD superseded function (tier.ps1 L242 states Get-WkSkillBaseScore replaces the old Get-WkTierScore loop). REAL formula: (1) not found OR stepCount at most 10 gives a flat 100. (2) stepCount 11 or more gives structural = min(85, plus 40 if a -howto sibling exists, plus 40 if a -ref sibling exists, plus 20 if a NAVIGATION or howto-naming step exists) -- the 3-tier requirement. (3) OVERSIZE-BASE DIVISION DECAY (skilllock.ps1 L152, the 20-over curve the USER built): structural times 20 divided by max(20, stepCount). So at most 20 steps gives times 1 (NO oversize penalty), and beyond 20 it decays inversely with step count (30 steps times 0.67, 40 steps times 0.5). The anchor is literally 20 -- the user raised it from 10 because 20 is the real Sonnet/Haiku-skimmable ceiling and dividing by 10 over-penalized 11-to-19-step skills. (4) plus a reflex-grade bonus 0 to 5, then an AGE-DECAY wrapper: final = round(struct times 0.99 to the power ageDays) -- a skill decays on its OWN mtime (about 74 at 30 days, about 60 at 50 days = the threshold), and reviving needs a substantive refresh, not a date-bump. So there are TWO stacked step pressures plus age: the 3-tier structural need starts at 11 steps, and the oversize division decay starts past 20 steps. The user 20-until-free then inverse-to-overage description was exactly the oversize term.

PHASE 5b -- THE CEILING-KNOCK GRADUATION PATH (user 2026-07-15), the second road into the STATIC tier. WHEN: a step has climbed to the position just below the === divider or a [PIN] and keeps being liked with nowhere left to rise. HOW: count the ceiling-knocks DEDUPED BY SESSION, and at 3 distinct sessions within a day, GRADUATE the step above the divider -- performing the move with the move-step verb, never the swap verb (see the CRITICAL note below). WHY, on three counts. (1) IT FILLS A REAL DEAD END, hit live on 2026-07-15: the 'verify an agent's claim' step of sonnet-reflection rose 6 to 5 to 2 to 1 across genuinely-earned likes and then returned 'like 1 out of range (valid range = 2..10)'. The step became unlikeable precisely BECAUSE it was the most valuable one, so the merit system had no way to register its continued proving -- and the forced move was to like some OTHER step that did not carry the mission, which is REFLEX-NOISE-INJECTION, the exact abuse the gates exist to stop. A gate whose success state makes its own payment impossible manufactures the dishonesty it polices. (2) THE SESSION-DEDUP IS LOAD-BEARING, not a detail: one session can knock a ceiling three times in five seconds, because the pulse gate DEMANDS a like but does not LIMIT likes -- so an un-deduped count is a 5-second forgery and violates the reward-proportional-to-forgery-cost law. Deduped by session it becomes expensive in the right way: three INDEPENDENT sessions must each judge that same step their most useful, which is structurally the same proof as PHASE 4 resurrection (independent agreement), merely compressed in time instead of spread across it. PHASE 1 already mandates exactly this dedup for like-counts, so the machinery exists. (3) THE THRESHOLD IS HIGHER THAN RESURRECTION'S FOR A REASON: resurrection additionally proves DURABILITY -- the reflex survived being archived and forgotten -- while a ceiling-knock proves only concurrent agreement and never tests whether the step outlives neglect. The STATIC tier is archive-IMMUNE and therefore permanent, so the weaker proof must clear a higher bar. The tier now has two entrances: RESURRECTION, slow, where TIME is the judge; and CEILING-KNOCK, fast, where CONSENSUS is the judge. CRITICAL IMPLEMENTATION NOTE: do NOT build this on the step-swap verb. That verb is a PHANTOM MUTATION -- it prints a success line and bumps the version while leaving the .skill.json BYTE-IDENTICAL (measured 2026-07-15 by reading the file back; filed as suggest ts=2026-07-15T10:47:44; now hard-blocked in the harness). Building graduation on it would produce a promotion that logs success and moves nothing -- the exact phantom class this whole workstream exists to kill. Use move-step N --to M, verified to actually persist by disk read-back. OWNERSHIP per the ARCHITECTURE SPLIT step: the counting and the graduation decision are HARNESS work; the === and [PIN] ceiling recognition inside like remains CORE's.

NAVIGATION (3-tier cluster, 2026-07-17): this T1 core holds the PHASE LAWS themselves (PHASE 1 rise / 2 sink / 3 archive / 4 resurrection / 5 static-tier + ceilings + the architecture split + score-pressure trigger). The step-by-step CURATION PROCEDURE the model runs on score-pressure (how to execute PHASE 3 sweep, PHASE 4 resurrection check, PHASE 5 graduation, and the tier-aware --like rule) -> wkappbot skill read reflex-merit-lifecycle-howto. The canonical edit-gate SCORE FORMULA, the dated build STATUS, and the PHASE 5b ceiling-knock incident -> wkappbot skill read reflex-merit-lifecycle-ref. Both siblings are part of this cluster.

DECISION: fusing two overlapping steps into one is a curation action distinct from PHASE 2/3 sink-and-archive, and this skill did not name it until now. WHEN: during a score-pressure curation pass, two steps in the core state the same underlying principle from different angles rather than one being simply stale or low-merit. HOW: do not archive either one to -ref as if it were noise -- read both in full, write ONE new step that states the shared principle once and folds both WHY incidents into a single WHY paragraph, then delete both originals. This differs from PHASE 3 (moving a genuinely stale, dated-incident-only step out of core) because both source steps here are still individually valid and worth keeping, just redundant with each other -- the fix is consolidation, not removal. Every fused (and every archived-to-ref, and every resurrected) step must still be written in the 4-slot TAG/WHEN/HOW/WHY shape enforced by the anti-knowledge reflex-format gate. TODO: add a self-test to wkharness-guards-stop-formatstrike.ps1 that constructs a fake draft-persistence summary string containing a verbatim formatPatterns trigger phrase inside a KNOWN_BUGS-style field value (mirroring wkharness-stop-draft.ps1's actual '[Already captured...] | KNOWN_BUGS: ...' join format), feeds it to Test-WkStopReasonIsFormatClass, and records whether it misclassifies -- this converts the still-open report-authorship self-poisoning risk (HANDOFF OPEN item 2) from a documented theory into either a confirmed bug or a confirmed non-issue, without changing any live behavior. -- see reflex-integrity-guard step 12 for the exact required shape and the four allowed TAG values. WHY: on 2026-07-18, sonnet-reflection carried an agent-claim-verification step and a brief-fact-verification step separately for the same discipline (checking before trusting) at two different moments of a delegation, and archiving either one to -ref would have been the WRONG move since both moments still needed covering in core -- fusing them into one step covering both moments made the core shorter AND kept the coverage, which sink-and-archive alone cannot do. Cross: reflex-integrity-guard (the 4-slot format every fused step must still satisfy).

DECISION: extend --like with an optional --why flag, implementable ENTIRELY on the harness side via existing CLI primitives, no wkappbot-core change needed. WHEN: a session pays a --like pulse and has a specific, articulable reason THIS particular event proved the step useful, distinct from prior like events on the same step. HOW: wkappbot skill read reflex-merit-lifecycle-howto for the current --like mechanics, then a harness hook intercepting a --like ... --why '<reason>' command shape can orchestrate two existing calls -- let the real --like run unchanged (the fragment anchor and reorder behave exactly as today), then resolve which step index it matched and issue a follow-up wkappbot skill edit <id> --step N --content '<original text> //reason1-<model>: <reason>' using the ALREADY-EXISTING in-place step-edit primitive (skill-edit-step-ordering-spec). FORMAT: each accumulated --why reason is appended as a comment-style marker distinct from the prose WHY text, numbered and model-tagged -- //reason1-<model>: <text>//reason2-<model>: <text>//reason3-<model>: <text> -- so the trail visibly separates the ORIGINAL authored reasoning from LATER cross-model endorsement evidence, and shows which model (Sonnet/Opus/Haiku/etc) found the step useful at each event, not just how many times. HOW (alternative, not recommended): a direct .skill.json field edit could achieve the same JSON result, but this repo's own harness:block rules already forbid raw .skill.json writes from any tool -- the --step N --content orchestration is the correct path, never a raw JSON edit. WHY: user-proposed 2026-07-19 as the clean resolution to a real design tension -- naively refreshing a liked step's CONTENT on every like would break the content-fragment anchor (this skill's own PHASE 1 note: a like lapses if the endorsed content is edited away), but appending only to WHY preserves the anchor while letting a step's evidence deepen every time it proves useful in a new context. CORRECTED twice same day: (1) originally scoped as a wkappbot-core CLI feature request, but the harness can orchestrate --like plus a follow-up --step N --content call using ALREADY-SHIPPED CLI primitives, no core change required; (2) the comment-marker model-tagged format (//reasonN-model: text) was added so accumulated reasons stay visually distinct from the original prose and carry per-model attribution.

DECISION: periodically consolidate accumulated //reasonN-model comment markers on a single step's WHY text once they grow noisy, mirroring the same batch-same-class-notes discipline this session's own reflection-core tending already follows. WHEN: a step's WHY text has accumulated many //reasonN-model markers (the --why accumulation design in this skill's own prior step) and the marker list itself has become long enough to be noise rather than signal. HOW: wkappbot skill read reflex-merit-lifecycle-howto for the accumulation mechanics, then apply whichever cleanup is simplest to implement -- EITHER fold the accumulated markers into one consolidated summary clause naming the distinct models/contexts that endorsed the step, OR the simpler ROLLING-WINDOW option: keep only the most recent 3 //reasonN-model markers and drop older ones outright, renumbering 1-3, since the most recent endorsements are the freshest signal and a fixed cap of 3 is cheap to implement mechanically with no summarization judgment required. WHY: user-proposed 2026-07-19 as a direct follow-up to the --why accumulation design -- an unbounded-growth marker trail would eventually re-create the exact oversize-decay noise problem this whole session spent effort curing at the whole-skill level, just relocated to the WHY clause of one step instead; the user then offered the keep-last-3 rolling window as an acceptable simpler alternative to full summarization.

PHASE 0 -- FALSITY IS NOT LOW MERIT, AND IT IS THE ONE CASE WHERE DELETION OR REWRITE BEATS ARCHIVING (owner directive 2026-08-02). Every other phase in this skill sorts knowledge by MERIT: a true-but-unused step sinks, gets archived to -ref, and may resurrect. That machinery is correct for knowledge that is merely unloved, and it is WRONG for knowledge that is FALSE. WHEN: you discover that a step, a claim, a comment, or a fixture states something that is not true of the current system. HOW: correct it IN PLACE with skill edit --find and --replace, or replace it with the measured truth, THE MOMENT you find it -- do not sink it, do not archive it, do not append a contradicting step beside it and leave both standing. Where the wrong thing is a code comment or a test expectation rather than a skill step, the same rule applies to that artifact. WHY THE ARITHMETIC FAVOURS ACTING, and this is the owner's point: a false step costs every future session that reads it, and it costs them at the worst moment -- while they are deciding what to do, with no reason to doubt it. That cost recurs forever and compounds, because a session that acts on it produces further work built on the error. Correcting it costs ONE edit, ONCE. There is no comparison, so there is no deliberation to have: the moment you know a thing is wrong, keeping it is the expensive option. TWO STEPS THAT WOULD OTHERWISE CONFLICT, reconciled here: harness-skill-delete-guard forbids DELETING A SKILL, and it is right -- a reflection is the accumulated record of what a model got wrong, and destroying the file destroys the only thing preventing recurrence. This phase is about a wrong CLAIM inside a skill, not the skill itself, and the delete-guard's own remedy says exactly this: if a skill is wrong, correct the step in place. Archive what is stale; rewrite what is false; never delete the record. MEASURED THE SAME DAY, four times in one shift: a Pending line claimed a Stop-pipeline audit was clean when the same defect sat inside the audited file; a self-test fixture asserted that an empty closing report should be ALLOWED, encoding a fail-open the owner had caught live that day, so any session greening the suite would have reverted the fix; a skill instructed a curl of a hardcoded CDP port the global rules forbid; and ROOT itself raised a false alarm about a scorer stub and had to correct it within the same turn. Each was cheap to fix on discovery and would have been expensive to leave. Cross: harness-skill-delete-guard (never delete the record), model-instruction-drift-why-the-harness-exists (a stale claim left standing is what a later session substitutes for measurement), on-load STALE-SKILL SPOT-FIX REFLEX (the same discipline stated for skills you merely happen to read).
